Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.values

Record Class MandelaRange

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.values.MandelaRange
Record Components:
from - the first value
to - the boundary
exclusive - true when to itself is not included
step - the stride, never zero; negative walks downward
public record MandelaRange(long from, long to, boolean exclusive, long step) extends Record
A Mandela range: a..b includes b, a..<b does not, and a..b step s produces every s-th value.

A range is a value, not a loop. It can be bound to a variable, stored in a map, passed to a function, tested with in, and iterated by for (i in 1..10). It never materialises its elements, so 0..1000000 costs the same as 0..10.

Ranges are integral. A Double bound makes the comparison rules unresolvable at the edges (which of 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 fall inside?), so Mandela requires integers and the compiler enforces it.

The stride is written the way Kotlin writes it, because a range is one of the places where the two languages are meant to feel the same to a host developer: 0..8 step 2 gives 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, and a negative stride walks down (8..0 step -2). A range whose direction contradicts its bounds is empty, which is the same rule 10..1 already follows, so there is no range that means two different things depending on how it is read.
